placements.caption: Core and accessory AMR genes show nearly identical baseline fitness distributions, indicating that conservation status does not predict laboratory fitness burden in this analysis.
Forest plot comparing essential-gene enrichment among core genes across the reported conservation–essentiality datasets.
Fitness–conservation relationships vary across gene classes and measurement contexts, showing a positive overall association alongside conditional reversals and weaker effects.
FBA versus TnSeq concordance across 866 genes, illustrating the reported 73.8% agreement between model predictions and measured phenotypes.
FBA–TnSeq concordance across 866 genes, illustrating the extent and limits of agreement between model predictions and disruption phenotypes.
PCA biplot showing the broad continuous phenotype axes and the carbon-source loadings that define them.
PCA variance explained across carbon-source conditions, illustrating the low-dimensional structure inferred from the deletion-phenotype landscape.
Conservation enrichment among trade-off genes shows that core or conserved genes can nevertheless exhibit substantial laboratory burden.
Burden varies across condition types, illustrating that core-gene coverage and laboratory fitness burden are distinct outcomes.
Threshold sensitivity analysis shows that binary essentiality agreement varies poorly across cutoffs despite more informative continuous fitness rankings.
Threshold-sensitivity analysis shows that binary essentiality calls are unstable across cutoffs and provide poorer agreement with complete-knockout lethality than continuous fitness.
Scatter plot and histogram showing the 57.0% fitness-flip rate between antibiotic and non-antibiotic conditions across 797 genes.
Antibiotic-versus-non-antibiotic fitness comparisons show the broad AMR condition-dependent signal, including the distribution underlying the reported 57.0% flip rate.
Fitness-flip distributions show the broad any-antibiotic signal linking AMR-gene effects across antibiotic and non-antibiotic conditions.
Phylogenetic control tests whether cofitness and co-inheritance associations persist beyond shared ancestry.
Phylogenetic control shows how cofitness–co-occurrence associations change after accounting for shared ancestry, clarifying the limits of inferring biological coupling.
Within-species AMR comparisons show that environmental effects are uncommon and heterogeneous after multiple-testing correction.
Within-species AMR differences across environments are limited and heterogeneous, underscoring the contrast with broader ecological associations.
Openness–AMR associations by phylum, illustrating positive stratified relationships that contrast with the near-zero pooled correlation.
AMR breadth versus pangenome openness across phyla, showing positive lineage-specific associations despite the near-zero pooled correlation.
Baseline fitness distributions are nearly identical for core and accessory AMR genes, showing that AMR conservation status need not predict knockout fitness cost.
Core and accessory AMR genes show nearly identical baseline knockout-fitness distributions, supporting decoupling between mechanism-associated conservation and baseline fitness burden.
Fitness-effect breadth versus conservation, showing how broadly acting and condition-specific fitness effects relate to gene conservation.
Pathway conservation differs by dependency class, illustrating why latent capability, active dependency, and essentiality are not interchangeable measures.
Complex I fitness deficit on aromatic versus non-aromatic substrates by NDH-2 status, showing no statistically supported general NDH-2 compensation pattern.
Complex I fitness effects differ between aromatic and non-aromatic conditions as a function of NDH-2 status, framing the evidence for ADP1-specific Complex I contributions.
Bridge summary showing the differing matched-strain and species coverage totals reported by the phenotype and isolation-environment analyses.
Bridge-summary comparison of strain- and GTDB-species coverage across the two BacDive analyses, highlighting their non-equivalent matched datasets.
MicrobeAtlas synthesis showing phylogenetic signal across trait–domain combinations and PGLS estimates for the association between metal-type diversity and inferred niche breadth.
Metal scores are substantially higher among isolates associated with heavy-metal contamination, illustrating the positive environmental association reported by BacDive.
Metal scores are higher in heavy-metal-contaminated environments, illustrating the positive BacDive association underlying the conservation-versus-ecology discrepancy.
Model comparison shows that taxonomy explains substantially more variance than phenotype features, with little improvement when phenotype is added to the taxonomic model.
Model comparison shows that taxonomy explains substantially more phenotype variance than phenotype features alone, with only a modest incremental gain from adding phenotypes to taxonomy.
Quality-filtered cultured deep-subsurface genomes show lower amino-acid pathway completeness and self-sufficiency than the comparison cohort.
Violin distributions compare self-sufficiency across cohorts, showing whether cultured deep-subsurface genomes exhibit elevated pathway completeness.
Four-panel synthesis showing the 547 enriched accessory orthologous groups alongside cohort structure and lineage- versus metric-specific signals in Bacillota_B.
Four-panel synthesis comparing the original marker-based iron-reduction result with the corrected functional-signal definitions, cohort patterns, and statistical tests.
Synthesis of the original and corrected iron-reduction marker analyses, showing how marker definitions alter the inferred depth-associated signal.
Schema-level linkage graph showing the breadth of cross-tenant bridges defined by shared canonical join keys, distinct from evidence of realized use.
Concordance and cross-database coverage for WoM-produced metabolites, highlighting the evidence behind the actionable Fitness Browser bridge.
Exploratory functional stress score versus contamination index by mapping mode, illustrating the coverage- and resolution-sensitive association.
Mapping and feature coverage by relaxed versus strict modes, providing context for the change in functional-association significance.
Conservation breadth across taxonomic and mobile categories reveals substantial variation that is obscured by near-universal eggNOG estimates.
Fitness–conservation gradient illustrating how laboratory growth costs can coexist with broad evolutionary retention of core genes.
Cost–benefit portrait illustrating how laboratory fitness costs can coexist with broad evolutionary retention.
Conservation varies across laboratory fitness profiles, showing that evolutionary retention is associated with—but not fully determined by—measured laboratory fitness.
Fitness–conservation gradient comparing laboratory deletion burden with evolutionary gene retention, highlighting the mismatch between measured fitness effects and core-genome status.
Fitness–conservation gradient showing the weak but consistent association between fitness effects and gene conservation in the broader analyses.
Distribution of core module genes, showing the 86.0% module-gene core fraction relative to the 81.5% genome-wide baseline.
Forest plot quantifying the enrichment of core status among essential genes, including the estimated effect and uncertainty.
Forest plot comparing core-gene enrichment among essential versus non-essential genes, including the reported odds ratio and uncertainty.
Coverage of phenotype, conservation, environmental, and neighborhood evidence across dark genes, illustrating why these evidence types can produce different priorities.
Comparison of overall dark genes with the residual truly dark subset, highlighting their differing evidence profiles and stress signals.
Coverage of dark-gene evidence shows the distinction between linked genes assessed for annotation and the larger set of unlinked genes that remains unevaluated.
Annotation tiers show how many dark genes remain hypothetical or lack sufficient linkage for functional assessment, underscoring the limits of the current evidence.
Partial correlation does not systematically increase with the fraction of environmental genomes, arguing that sampling composition alone does not explain the weak environment–gene-content signal.
Partial correlations by species group show the reanalysis results and their variability across environmental and Human-associated species, supporting a weak relationship despite sampling asymmetries.
Ten organism–condition experiments provide evidence for 242 of 500 dark genes, illustrating the immediate yield of exploiting organisms with dense informative profiles.
Evidence coverage varies across organisms, illustrating how unequal condition panels can bias functional-gene prioritization toward well-profiled organisms.
DvH fitness-profile correlations with NaCl show that metal–NaCl associations vary substantially across metals, despite shared-stress analyses.
Pangenome openness is associated with the latent rate of metabolic capability across species, supporting metabolic variation as a candidate determinant or proxy.
Pangenome openness shows no significant relationship with the tested environmental and phylogenetic effects in the harmonized analysis.
COG differentiation significance across all analyzed species, illustrating widespread functional structure rather than a single leakage-like pattern.

Relationship between the fraction of genome-wide gene-content variation attributed to environment and partial environmental correlations across species, illustrating the distinction between environmental dominance and statistical significance.

Continuous relationship between the fraction of environmental gene-content effects and partial correlation strength, illustrating why environmental dominance by effect size need not imply widespread statistical significance.
Confirmatory defense scores show no robust contamination association across mapping modes, illustrating the aggregate-analysis null result.
Confirmatory defense-versus-contamination associations remain null or weak across mapping modes despite differing coverage.
Partial correlations by species group show that environmental associations are detectable but generally small and vary across groups.
Mean embedding distance increases monotonically with geographic distance, supporting a geographic structure in the embedding despite uncertainty about its genome-level ecological interpretation.
Ecotype correlation summary comparing environmental and phylogenetic associations, showing that phylogeny generally provides the stronger predictor of genome-wide gene-content similarity.
Variance partitioning shows weak whole-genome environmental structure alongside stronger, localized prophage-module associations across environments.
Distribution of partial correlations across species, illustrating the generally weak environmental structure detected in the whole-genome reanalysis.
Comparison of environmental and host/phylogenetic contributions to genome-wide gene-content similarity, illustrating the dominance of phylogeny in the ecotype analysis.
Partial correlations by species group show no stronger environment–gene-content association for environmental species than for human-associated species.
Synthesis of environment-associated microbial traits, showing phylogenetic signal across trait domains and PGLS estimates for metal-linked functional associations.
Distribution of environmental partial correlations, illustrating the predominantly weak gene-content associations reported in the ecotype reanalysis.
Discovery funnel showing how occurrence and predicted capability narrow candidate taxa but do not by themselves demonstrate in situ compound catabolism.
Genus-resolved distribution of 3-hydroxybenzoic-acid utilizer taxa, illustrating their high environmental prevalence while not by itself establishing in situ catabolic activity.
PCA of Pseudomonas pathway profiles by isolation environment, illustrating environmental structure alongside lineage-associated separation.
Distribution of pathway dependency classes, showing that broader pathway capability includes active, latent, and intermediate pathways rather than uniformly measured fitness requirements.
Distribution of pathway dependency classes, highlighting 57 active dependencies (35.4%) and 66 latent capabilities (41.0%) in the broader metabolic-capability analysis.
Summary comparison of overall dark genes and the residual truly dark subset, highlighting how stress associations and other evidence patterns change with subset definition.
Synthesis of environmental metal associations, showing trait–domain phylogenetic signal (Pagel’s λ) alongside PGLS effect estimates.
Multi-organism comparison of metal cross-resistance, highlighting strong pangenome-scale signals alongside weak or null species-scale validation.
Gene-level literature coverage is highly skewed: many genes have no text-mined paper link, while linked genes commonly have only one paper.
Gene coverage is highly uneven: most genes have few or no text-mined paper links, while a small subset accounts for a disproportionate share of the literature evidence.
PGP gene co-occurrence heatmap highlighting the strong pqqC–acdS association and statistically significant pairwise enrichments.
AMR–prophage distance distribution and cumulative fraction, showing that only 10.4% of AMR instances lie within 10 genes of a strict prophage marker.
Across phyla, defense-system counts increase with prophage-cluster burden, illustrating the reported system-level arms-race association.
FBA flux predictions and TnSeq essentiality calls were concordant for 639 of 866 genes (73.8%), with 227 discordant genes highlighting candidates for model refinement or regulatory effects.
Pairwise correlations of mutant growth fitness across eight carbon sources show that urea fitness is largely independent of the other conditions, especially quinate.
Growth defect distributions across the eight carbon sources reveal demanding, moderate, and robust condition tiers.
Hierarchically ordered growth profiles across 2,034 genes show broadly sensitive and tolerant patterns alongside the small quinate-specific aromatic degradation module.
Contingency table and defect rates show that FBA class is not associated with quantitative growth defects among TnSeq-dispensable genes.
Condition-specific FBA flux has weak and mixed correlations with measured mutant growth across carbon sources.
MSA depth is substantially higher in core gene clusters, which also have lower hypothetical-protein rates and a smaller structurally novel fraction than accessory classes.
AMR-containing ICA modules are larger than non-AMR modules, with coverage summarized across resistance mechanisms.
GO-term Jaccard similarities show that AMR support networks are more similar across mechanisms within an organism than across organisms.
AMR gene-cluster diversity differs substantially by ecological environment, with clinical and human-gut species showing the highest median counts.
AMR resistance-mechanism composition varies by environment, with metal resistance enriched in soil and aquatic species and target modification enriched in clinical and human-gut species.
Forest plot showing the positive relative fitness shift of AMR gene knockouts versus non-AMR knockouts across 25 organisms and the pooled random-effects estimate.
Distribution and condition-paired comparison of AMR gene fitness flips, showing that AMR genes generally become more important under antibiotic exposure.
AMR genes are substantially less conserved in the core genome than the pangenome baseline and are enriched in accessory genomes.
AMR conservation varies strongly by mechanism, with intrinsic beta-lactamases and efflux systems more core-associated than acquired resistance genes.
Variation landscape summarizing AMR prevalence classes, variability in relation to pangenome openness, Jaccard diversity across phyla, and prevalence by resistance mechanism.
Resistance-island co-occurrence analysis showing island-size distributions, observed versus null co-inheritance strength, and the number of islands per species.
The integrated pipeline resolved 96 of 201 gapfilled reaction–organism pairs (47.8%), including 44 high-confidence assignments.
Leave-one-out comparisons show that the full evidence pipeline outperformed each individual evidence stream and remained more effective when any one component was removed.
The 51 quinate-specific genes partition into aromatic-pathway, Complex I, iron-acquisition, PQQ-biosynthesis, and regulatory support categories, with Complex I forming the largest subsystem.
FBA predicts higher Complex I-associated flux on aromatic substrates than in the comparison condition despite assigning no Complex I genes as essential.
Metal tolerance scores are highest among heavy-metal contamination isolates, with progressively smaller effects across waste/sludge, all-contamination, and industrial environments.
The BacDive–GTDB pangenome bridge summarizes strain matching, species coverage, and the contribution of exact versus suffix-normalized species-name matches.
Univariate effect sizes for BacDive phenotype associations with genome-based metal tolerance, highlighting Gram stain, oxidase, motility, urease, enzyme breadth, nitrate reduction, and catalase.
Phylogenetic-blocked cross-validation shows that taxonomy and metal-resistance gene counts outperform phenotype-only models for predicting metal tolerance.

Four-panel synthesis of deep-clay Bacillota_B specialization, including enriched anaerobic and persistence functions, larger genome and OG complements, and the corrected multi-heme cytochrome comparison.
Agency-by-topic coverage heatmap showing DOE-BER’s broad topic reach and the concentration of biological data across funding programs.
Tenant–topic linkage graph showing the 536 schema-level cross-tenant bridges identified through shared canonical join keys.
Master synthesis of the Fur-, ChvI-, envelope-transport, peptidoglycan, and comparative-genomics evidence supporting the proposed mechanism of Δfur ΔsspB-dependent ΔlpxC viability.
Leaden Δfur logFC versus the present 4584-vs-4580 response, highlighting concordant, buffered, and discordant genes.
PA14 preferentially utilizes amino acids, especially proline, histidine, and ornithine, under synthetic cystic-fibrosis sputum conditions.
Carbon-utilization patterns across isolates reveal substrate-specific metabolic variation relevant to competition with PA14.
Sulfate-reduction markers are enriched in the cultured deep-clay cohort, supporting a porewater rather than rock-attached community signature.
Anaerobic toolkit scores are highest in deep-clay genomes but much lower in shallow-clay and soil cohorts.
Across organisms, cofit gene pairs show only a small but statistically significant increase in co-occurrence relative to prevalence-matched random pairs.
ICA modules exhibit stronger co-inheritance than prevalence-matched null modules, supporting coordinated multi-gene regulation as a constraint on pangenome variation.
Across 194,216 genes from 43 bacteria, genes with stronger measured fitness effects tend to be more conserved, although even genes without detectable effects are frequently core.
The selection-signature matrix shows how laboratory fitness costs and pangenome conservation combine to distinguish costly, conserved genes from costly-and-dispensable and other categories.
Distribution of linked genes across core, auxiliary, and singleton pangenome clusters, showing that 82.0% were classified as core.
Forest plot comparing core-genome enrichment among essential and non-essential genes across organisms, with a median odds ratio of 1.56.
Core genes show greater laboratory fitness burden than non-core genes in Protein Metabolism, Motility, and RNA Metabolism, while Cell Wall genes show the opposite pattern.
Trade-off genes are enriched among core genes, comprising 17.8% of genes examined and showing a significant conservation association.
SEED category enrichment highlights the strong overrepresentation of mobile genetic elements and depletion of core cellular functions among costly+dispensable genes.
Costly+dispensable genes have narrower ortholog breadth and a much higher orphan-gene fraction than costly+conserved genes, consistent with recent acquisition.
Heatmap showing the extent of shared NaCl and metal-important gene signals across organisms and metals.
Chloride concentration is not correlated with metal–NaCl gene overlap, supporting the conclusion that chloride is not the primary confounder.
Summary of partial correlations showing that phylogenetic similarity generally predicts gene-content similarity more strongly than environmental similarity across the 172 species.
Distribution of environmental and phylogenetic effects across ecological categories, highlighting the generally weak environmental signal and stronger phylogenetic influence.
Partial correlations show substantial overlap between Environmental and Human-associated species, with no significant group difference (Mann–Whitney U, p=0.83).
The fraction of environmental genomes per species is not associated with partial-correlation strength (Spearman ρ=-0.085, p=0.25).
Heatmap showing significant COG differentiation across the 12 species and COG categories, demonstrating that every species has differentiated functions.
Effect-size distributions show that adaptive COG categories generally exhibit larger ecotype shifts than housekeeping categories.
Discovery funnel showing the progression from 83 enrichment compounds to structure-resolved, KEGG-linked, callable, and organism-dark compounds.
Odds-ratio forest plot showing the strongest cross-compound utilization associations and their uncertainty intervals.
Confirmatory defense score shows no robust association with the contamination index across genus-level mapping modes.
Exploratory functional stress-score associations with contamination vary by mapping mode and provide limited evidence for a coverage-adjusted defense trend.
Sample-level ordination shows community separation by hydrogeological zone and well, supporting zone as a major driver of sediment community structure.
Genus-inferred biogeochemical process hotspots across the SSO grid highlight oxidative activity near U3, denitrification near M5, and an inferred anaerobic zone near M6.
Embedding cosine distance increases with geographic separation, with a substantially stronger gradient for environmental than human-associated samples.
The AlphaEarth subset is dominated by human-associated genomes, especially clinical and gut samples, while individual environmental categories are smaller.
Overview of ortholog-family essentiality across 48 bacteria, showing universally essential, variably essential, and never-essential families.
Conservation architecture of essentiality classes, highlighting the contrasting core-genome fractions of universal, variable, never-essential, and orphan essential genes.
GapMind pathway-completeness results show that all seven organisms contain 17 of 18 amino-acid biosynthesis pathways, with serine biosynthesis incomplete only in *Desulfovibrio vulgaris*.
Distribution of GOTTCHA2-derived eukaryotic fractions across runs, including the predominance of plastid sequences among detected eukaryotic signal.
Core-genome percentages for genes important under each condition class, compared with the all-gene baseline.
ROC curves show that field or lab fitness alone weakly predicts core-genome status, while adding gene length improves prediction.
Core conservation increases across fitness-importance profiles, with essential and frequently deleterious genes substantially more conserved than generally neutral genes.
Core genes have heavier fitness-effect tails in both negative and positive directions than auxiliary genes, indicating stronger costs and benefits under tested conditions.
Within-module fitness correlations are significantly stronger than background correlations across the 1,116 ICA modules, validating their cofitness structure.
Cross-organism module families reveal conserved fitness modules spanning multiple organisms, including families extending across much of the 32-organism panel.
Evidence coverage across the 57,011 dark genes, including pangenome links, strong fitness effects, essentiality, and fitness-module membership.
GapMind pathway gaps and associated strongly fitness-active dark genes across analyzed organisms.
Concordance categories and cross-database coverage summarize how the 58 WoM-produced metabolites were supported across Fitness Browser, BacDive, and GapMind.
Significant Fitness Browser gene effects reveal the differing genetic complexity of metabolism across WoM-produced metabolites.
Producer × participation scores across taxonomic ranks define the four ecological-agora behavior classes.
Bacteroidota PUL positions relative to other phyla show that the absolute-zero Innovator-Exchange criterion is not met, while a small relative HGT signal remains.
Overlap of experimental conditions across the four integrated datasets, highlighting the shared basis for cross-dataset genotype–phenotype comparisons.
PCA of KO presence/absence profiles showing eight metabolic guilds across the 123 strains and their relationship to taxonomy.
Warming increased Actinobacteria and decreased Acidobacteria in organic soil, reproducing the reported community-level taxonomic response.
Cross-cutting synthesis of the rigor-controlled target decision matrix, per-patient cocktail design, and clinical-translation roadmap.
UC Davis patient ecotype assignments compared with the reference ecotype framework.
Genus-level groundwater abundance associations with uranium concentration, highlighting significant positive and negative relationships after multiple-testing correction.
Community composition differs between high- and low-uranium groundwater sites, indicating broader ecological restructuring.
Across phyla, xoxF calls greatly outnumber mxaF calls, demonstrating the broad dominance of lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase markers.
xoxF-associated cassette prevalence varies by environment, with the strongest statistically supported enrichment in soil and sediment and a secondary enrichment in marine settings.
16S genus composition shows the strong bacterial restructuring caused by lignin enrichment and the distinct copiotrophic assemblage produced by labile-carbon supplementation.
16S PCoA shows persistent separation of communities according to their Round-1 carbon history, supporting ecological memory and non-convergence under shared Round-2 conditions.
Pathway dependency classes differ markedly by category, with carbon-source utilization more often latent or intermediate and amino-acid biosynthesis predominantly active.
Across species clades, latent capability rate increases with pangenome openness (Spearman ρ = 0.69, p < 0.001).
Multi-organism gene-level fitness correlations show predominantly positive cross-resistance across metal pairs.
Cross-resistance correlation strengths remain consistently positive across organisms, with the strongest conservation for Co–Ni and related divalent-metal pairs.
Core-genome fractions are higher among metal-important genes, with essential metals showing stronger core enrichment than toxic metals.
Conserved ortholog families span multiple organisms and metals, with broader metal phenotypes associated with greater pangenome conservation.
Specificity breakdown shows that metal-specific genes comprise the largest category across organisms, alongside general-sick and metal-plus-stress genes.
Core-gene enrichment is evident across all categories, with metal-specific genes showing a more modest enrichment than general-sick genes.
Synthesis of phylogenetic signal across traits and the positive PGLS association between metal-type diversity and bacterial niche breadth.
Robustness summary showing positive metal-type effects across key analyses, rarefaction coefficient stability, and the limited power of the archaeal analysis.
Distribution of module core-gene fractions, showing that most modules are predominantly core and summarizing the core, mixed, and accessory categories.
Family breadth is not associated with conservation: module-family core fraction remains essentially unchanged across the number of organisms spanned.

Across 13 testable amino-acid pathways, community pathway completeness was negatively associated with ambient metabolite intensity for 11 pathways, with leucine and arginine surviving false-discovery-rate correction.
PCA of community pathway completeness separates Soil, Freshwater, and Unknown ecosystem samples, with PC1 and PC2 explaining 49.4% and 16.6% of variance, respectively.
Scale comparison of NMDC-labeled resources by provenance class, highlighting the roughly 3,000-fold difference between the genuine NMDC biosample set and the co-hosted NCBI mirror.
Snapshot dates show that data currency varies across NMDC-labeled resources and is distributed across several months.
Pangenome openness shows no significant relationship with either environmental or phylogenetic effects on gene-content variation.
Lorenz curves show extreme inequality in literature coverage across organisms and genes, with organism-level concentration substantially exceeding gene-level concentration.
The protein-family literature coverage landscape reveals the large fraction of dark and dimly studied families alongside the small number of heavily studied families.

The 161 organism–pathway pairs divide into Active Dependency, Latent Capability, Incomplete but Important, and Missing categories, demonstrating that genomic completeness and observed fitness dependence are distinct.
Condition-type shifts show that all 66 Latent Capability pairs become fitness-important under at least one condition, most often nitrogen limitation, stress, or carbon limitation.
Co-occurrence analysis shows significant positive and negative associations among focal PGP genes, including the strong pqqC–acdS association and nifH separation from pqqC and hcnC.
PGP gene prevalence and log2 odds ratios show strong soil/rhizosphere enrichment of acdS, pqqC, and hcnC and depletion of nifH.
Defense-system prevalence varies substantially across bacterial phyla, with CRISPR-Cas and BREX widespread and CBASS comparatively rare.
Defense-system count is positively associated with prophage-cluster burden across species, supporting a broad arms-race pattern.
PHB pathway prevalence is strongly concentrated in a small set of phyla, led by Pseudomonadota, Myxococcota, and Halobacteriota.
Genome size is associated with PHB presence and niche breadth, yet PHB enrichment across environments persists within genome-size quartiles.
Heatmap of refined marker enrichment across root, rhizosphere, and phyllosphere compartments, illustrating statistically significant but modest compartment-specific differences.
Core-versus-accessory gene-cluster distributions show that beneficial PGP functions are more core-encoded than pathogenic functions.
Contingency analysis shows the modest prophage-proximity association with AMR accessory status and its dependence on the gene-distance threshold.
Across 4,770 species, prophage marker density is positively associated with AMR repertoire breadth in a log-log regression.
Variance partitioning shows that genome size dominates prophage-module composition, while environment explains additional variation beyond family-level phylogeny.
Constrained module-by-environment enrichment analysis highlights significant overrepresentation of structural and anti-defense modules in human-associated environments.
Heatmap of carbon-pathway completeness across species, ordered by subgenus and lifestyle, highlighting the concentration of sugar-pathway loss in host-associated lineages.
PCA of carbon-pathway profiles colored by isolation environment, showing a significant but overlapping ecological signal.
Growth-ratio heatmap showing that respiratory-chain component requirements differ qualitatively across carbon sources.
NADH production by substrate, including total yield and NADH per carbon, illustrating why concentrated quinate flux can increase Complex I dependence despite lower overall NADH production.
Summary comparison showing that truly dark genes are shorter, less core, less conserved, and more often essential than annotation-lag genes.
Annotation-clue tiers show that only 3.8% of truly dark genes have no detected clues, while most retain partial evidence for prioritization.
Heatmap of metabolite profiles for ENIGMA isolates grown in R2A medium, highlighting increased versus de novo-emerged metabolites.
Per-rank score distributions show how accessory functional acquisition varies across control classes and phylogenetic depth.
Pathway dependency classes distinguish realized metabolic dependence from latent or incomplete genomic capability.
Across 25 organisms, AMR-gene knockouts show a reproducible relative fitness shift compared with the non-AMR knockout background, while remaining below zero on average.
Fitness effects for AMR genes frequently flip toward greater importance under antibiotic exposure, illustrating the condition dependence of resistance fitness.
Core and accessory AMR genes have nearly identical baseline fitness effects, providing no evidence that pangenome prevalence explains measured AMR cost.
Fitness–conservation gradient showing that stronger laboratory fitness effects are associated with greater pangenome retention, but only modestly.
Core genes remain phenotypically active, including substantial fractions with positive or condition-dependent deletion effects.
Deletion growth-defect distributions across carbon sources demonstrate strong condition dependence in laboratory fitness.
Coverage of dark genes across annotation, phenotype, conservation, and other evidence layers, illustrating that functional darkness is layered rather than binary.
Distribution of condition classes among dark genes with strong phenotypes, showing that fitness effects are often context-dependent.
Forest plot comparing essential and non-essential genes across core-genome categories, showing that conservation helps prioritize essential genes but is not a complete explanation of function.
COG differentiation significance across species shows recurring, functionally nonrandom gene-content structure in 12 of 15 species.
Partial correlations by species group show weak broad-scale environment–gene-content associations, including the lower median signal in environmental species.
Across bacteria, increasing gene fitness importance is associated with higher pangenome conservation, but the relationship is modest rather than deterministic.
Laboratory deletion burden differs between core and non-core genes across functional categories, revealing the core-gene burden paradox and its exceptions.
Cofitness analysis identifies coordinated functional modules whose sizes and mechanistic coverage support conservation at the level of processes as well as individual genes.
Costly and dispensable genes have markedly narrower ortholog breadth and a higher orphan fraction than costly and conserved genes, indicating weak conservation of much burdensome accessory DNA.
A four-panel synthesis shows that deep-clay Bacillota genomes are larger than baseline genomes and have distinct accessory-gene enrichment despite comparable completeness.
Ecotype correlation analyses show that phylogeny generally explains genome-wide gene-content similarity better than environmental similarity.
Core and accessory AMR fractions differ across environments, with clinical species carrying a substantially larger accessory component than soil species.
Fitness effects of AMR genes shift between antibiotic-exposed and non-antibiotic conditions, illustrating condition-dependent resistance importance.
Cross-resistance heatmap showing predominantly positive, but metal-pair-dependent, fitness correlations across organisms.
AMR diversity and burden differ substantially across clinical, soil, aquatic, and animal-associated environments.
AMR genes are disproportionately enriched in the accessory genome relative to the general pangenome, while retaining a conserved intrinsic component.
Fitness effects of AMR genes shift toward greater importance under antibiotic exposure, illustrating condition-dependent resistance benefits.
COG differentiation rates across species and functional categories, distinguishing adaptive, housekeeping, and other signals.
Comparison of environmental and host effects on ecotype gene-content structure across species.
Relationship between fitness-effect magnitude and gene conservation, illustrating the tension between functional importance and core-genome retention.
Tenant–topic linkage graph showing the broad cross-tenant connection surface defined by shared canonical join keys.
Scale of NMDC-labeled resources by provenance class, illustrating why resource labels alone do not establish authority or comparability.
Consistency heatmap across Web of Microbes, Fitness Browser, BacDive, and GapMind, showing endpoint-level agreement and partial concordance.
Scale and provenance classes of NMDC-labeled resources, showing why name-based discovery must distinguish maintained authority and resource type.
Cross-tenant linkage graph showing potential schema connections based on shared canonical join keys, not yet validated biological integrations.
Discovery funnel showing the attrition from structure-resolved compounds to KEGG-linked and callable compounds in the ENIGMA carbon census.
FBA and TnSeq essentiality show how genome-scale metabolic capability compares with experimentally observed dependency across conditions.
The BERDL tenant–topic linkage graph illustrates how shared canonical identifiers create potential cross-dataset integration pathways.
A multi-layer synthesis of transcriptomic, proteomic, RB-TnSeq, regulon, and comparative-annotation evidence reveals distinct early and late responses to lipid-A loss.
Within-module cofitness correlations are stronger than background correlations, supporting the presence of structured, condition-dependent modules.
Module-level co-inheritance shows how coordinated gene groups provide a stronger genome-wide occurrence signal than isolated pairwise cofitness links.
Cross-organism module families vary in size and taxonomic span, illustrating both the portability and organism-specific limits of module conservation.
Dependency classes differ by pathway category, with latent capability substantially more common among carbon-utilization than amino-acid biosynthesis pathways.
Latent capability rates increase with pangenome openness, linking metabolic ecotype variation to genomic flexibility.
Pathway-completeness profiles illustrate why encoded capacity is evidence of potential rather than proof of metabolic independence.
FBA-predicted fluxes for quinate-specific genes show how respiratory demand changes with carbon source and metabolic architecture.
Concordance categories and database coverage quantify how matched metabolite production evidence supports, but does not prove, metabolic exchange.
AMR genes are substantially less conserved than the surrounding pangenome, demonstrating their enrichment in accessory genomic compartments.
Phylogenetic signal organizes AMR composition and burden, with AMR similarity tracking genomic relatedness across species.
Cross-resistance varies by metal pair, revealing a broadly shared but chemistry-dependent stress-response architecture.
Distribution of detected eukaryotic read fractions across workflow runs, showing the source split and prevalence of low-level eukaryotic signal.
Scale and provenance classes of resources carrying NMDC labels, illustrating why resource names alone do not establish provenance.
Discovery funnel from structure-resolved compounds to KEGG-linked and callable carbon-utilization evidence, highlighting the gap between potential and realized function.
Cumulative resolution of 201 gapfilled reaction–organism pairs, broken down by evidence-confidence level.
Comparison of predictive models showing that taxonomy contributed more explanatory power than phenotype features alone.
Growth-defect distributions across carbon sources show that gene essentiality varies continuously and condition-specifically.
Essential genes are enriched among conserved core genes, but the comparison shows that core status is not a sufficient proxy for essentiality.
Mutant growth distributions by FBA-predicted class illustrate where metabolic-network predictions agree with or diverge from measured condition-dependent fitness.
Essentiality changes across rich and minimal media, demonstrating that gene dependency is condition-specific.
Pathway-completeness results show that conserved metabolic capacity does not by itself establish condition-specific dependency.
FBA-predicted flux and mutant growth rates across carbon sources reveal that flux demand and gene essentiality can diverge.
Growth-defect severity varies substantially across the eight carbon sources, demonstrating that gene essentiality is conditional rather than binary.
PCA of ADP1 gene fitness profiles reveals shared growth-burden axes alongside substrate-specific condition loadings.
NaCl–metal overlap varies across organisms and metals, separating shared stress sensitivity from stressor-specific dependencies.
PCA biplot showing how carbon-source conditions separate gene-level growth sensitivities and condition loadings, illustrating that metabolic requirements are environmentally conditional.
Cumulative resolution and confidence breakdown of annotation gaps, showing that many gapfilled reaction–organism pairs remain unresolved at the gene level.
PCA biplot of ADP1 gene fitness profiles across carbon sources, showing multidimensional condition-specific requirements.
Comparison of FBA-predicted essentiality and transposon fitness, illustrating limited concordance between computational and insertion-based essentiality measures.
Per-metal classification of shared-stress versus metal-specific fitness requirements across organisms.
Fitness–conservation gradient showing that laboratory cost and long-term genomic conservation can coexist, revealing the core-genome burden paradox.
